findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to not be reaching the sanitizing concentration benchmark set by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm of quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- PIC made bleach water sanitizer at a concentration of 200 ppm. Inspector will return on 10/30/25 to check one of two solutions:
1) The facility has adjusted the water heater to reach 75F to allow quaternary ammonia sanitizer tablets to dissolve.
2) Facility has obtained unscented bleach (with an EPA registration number and label indicating use for food contact surfaces) to use as sanitizer. Facility has test strips for both sanitizers, so either are acceptable means of sanitation for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items (orange juice and heavy whipping cream) to be without date marking in the facility. CORRECTED- the heavy whipping cream was voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC), and the orange juice was labeled with a date. Ensure all TCS food and drinks are marked with a date once opened; the day the item is opened counts as “day one”. Use or discard within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed container holding multiple food contact utensils at the bar to be soiled with debris. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized cup holding utensils. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may transfer to food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Fan covers in the walk in cooler were observed to be soiled with dust and ice. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of debris. Clean fans during defrost. Inspector will check the cleaning of the fans during a spot check on 10/30/25.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]
